title: Noor and the Extraction
premise: Noor Quintana, a crash investigator who lost her family in an unattributed accident and lives under the name Oscar to stay invisible, discovers the safe house she's hidden in for six years has been listed online — with interior photos that reveal her false identity to whoever is hunting her. Following the listing to a corrupt real-estate pipeline, she uncovers a plot to stage a catastrophic 'accident' at a border checkpoint, timed to the shift change when oversight is thinnest. With help from Amara, a former colleague who becomes her found family and reluctant love, Noor races to expose the attack while wrestling with the inheritance her family left her: a duty to truth that staying invisible would betray. In the end she stops the attack at the checkpoint itself, chooses love over the safety of anonymity, and finally claims her real name in the official record.
about_author: Lena Blackwood is a former aviation insurance adjuster who spent a decade reading accident reports before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose careful lives are dismantled by a single overlooked document.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Noor, living quietly as 'Oscar Quintana' in a rural safe house, scrolls late-night listings and freezes: her house, her kitchen, her father's watch on the counter. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the vertigo of invisibility ending — six years of careful anonymity collapsing in one photograph.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: A flashback braided into present-day casework: the crash that killed Noor's family, ruled 'unattributed' by a report she was never allowed to read. She contacts her old handler, who warns her to run. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing, the first hint that her family's death was never an accident.

chapters.title: Amara
chapters.summary: Noor reaches out to Amara Reyes, a former colleague now at the transport authority, pretending it's routine. Amara recognizes her instantly — and covers for her instead of reporting her. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: wary tenderness; two women deciding to trust each other against protocol.

chapters.title: Sold to the Highest Bidder
chapters.summary: Tracing the listing, Noor finds the safe house sold through a shell company that has bought three other 'retired' safe houses — all near border infrastructure. Someone is mapping protected people and protected places. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: cold clarity; fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Shift Change
chapters.summary: Amara pulls checkpoint rosters and finds the pattern: every targeted site sits near a checkpoint whose shift change creates a ninety-minute oversight gap. A maintenance 'upgrade' is scheduled at the Del Rio crossing. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: dread as the abstract threat takes a date, a time, a place.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Noor opens the sealed box her family's lawyer held for her: her mother's investigation notes into the same shell company, unfinished. The inheritance isn't money — it's the case her mother died carrying. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: love against duty; she realizes finishing the work honors her family better than hiding ever did.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: The hunters find her — a staged break-in, a dead drop burned, her handler unreachable. Amara insists on staying despite the risk, and the two cross a line from allies into something more. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: intimacy forged under threat; choosing each other with no guarantee of tomorrow.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: They reconstruct the attack: a tanker rerouted through Del Rio during the shift gap, disguised as a routine accident. But the evidence is circumstantial, and going official exposes Amara. They have one window to act. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: the cost of duty — reporting means sacrificing the life they've just built.

chapters.title: Del Rio
chapters.summary: Climax. Noor goes to the checkpoint herself, using her mother's notes to force an unscheduled inspection while Amara triggers the paper trail upstream. The tanker is stopped minutes from the gap; the shell company's fixer is caught in the open. POV: alternating, converging. Emotional beat: terror, resolve, and the moment duty and love stop being opposites.

chapters.title: Noor Quintana
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the official report names the conspiracy — and names its lead investigator: Noor Quintana, not Oscar. She signs her real name, visits row twelve's memorial with Amara beside her, and closes her mother's file for good. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; invisibility traded for a life that is seen, shared, and finally her own.
